reasons: Claimed status is supported: § 3.5 (Effect of Termination) addresses only accrued payment obligations, and the cited paragraph contains no transition-assistance, data-return, export or deletion language, so the insert-type finding is correctly characterized as a deviation by omission in a hosting agreement holding Customer Content.

Redline is a clean, minimal insertion: the original sentences of p0049 are left untouched and a single new sentence tracks the playbook model language (six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in machine-readable format, deletion plus written certification), with the counterparty correctly named as IBM and the defined term 'Content' used.
Placement in § 3.5 is sensible and internally consistent — the finding notes § 3.5 survives termination under § 14.2, so the obligation is enforceable post-termination.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, carries the [Playbook] prefix, explains the change and rationale, and offers the 90-day fallback as the playbook directs.

Minor drafting note only (not disqualifying): clause (b) conditions the 30-day return on 'Customer's request' whereas the preferred position states an unconditional 30-day return; consider deleting 'of Customer's request' so the export deadline runs from termination.
